faqs: How much does the Kimi API cost?

On the Kimi API platform, read November 26, 2026, kimi-k3.1-pro costs $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens, with cached input at $0.20. kimi-k3 costs $3.00 and $15.00, and kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed $4.00 and $20.00. Prices exclude taxes.

No. A minimum recharge of $1 is needed to start using the API. When an account's cumulative recharge reaches $5, Kimi gives a $5 voucher, according to its recharge and rate limits page. Billing is pay as you go with no subscription plan.
When are Kimi K2 models retired?

The pricing page says K2 models stopped being available to newly registered users from October 31, 2026, that existing users are not affected, and that Moonshot plans to retire all K2 series models by the end of December 2026 (the page says "We plan"). No exact day is given.
Does the Kimi API have a batch discount?

Yes. kimi-k3.1-pro and kimi-k3 support batch inference billed at 60% of the standard price, for tasks that do not need real-time responses. On K3.1 Pro that is $1.20 per million input and $6.00 per million output tokens, on our arithmetic.
What are the Kimi API rate limits?

Limits depend on cumulative recharge. Tier0 ($1) allows 1 concurrent request, 3 requests per minute and 1,500,000 tokens a day. Tier1 ($10) allows 15 concurrent, 100 per minute, 2,000,000 tokens per minute and no daily cap. Tier5 ($3,000) allows 100 concurrent and 300 per minute.
Is Kimi cheaper on Together AI?

Not at standard prices. Together AI lists Kimi K3.1 Pro at $2.00 and $10.00 and Kimi K3 at $3.00 and $15.00 per million tokens, the same as the Kimi platform on November 26, 2026. Together's US geo-pinned rows cost 25% more.
body:
Short answer. On the Kimi API platform run by Moonshot AI, kimi-k3.1-pro costs $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens, with cached input at $0.20. kimi-k3 costs $3.00 and $15.00. Batch jobs are billed at 60% of the standard price, and you need a $1 top-up to start. Prices were read from the Kimi API pricing page on November 26, 2026; they exclude taxes.

The dated change is the K2 series. The page says that from October 31, 2026, K2 models "will no longer be available to newly registered users", and that Moonshot plans "to retire all K2 series models by the end of December 2026". If an agent still calls kimi-k2.6 or kimi-k2.7-code, moving it to K3.1 Pro raises the list price from $0.95 and $4.00 to $2.00 and $10.00 per million tokens. For a hypothetical chatbot with 10,000 conversations a month, that is $39 against $90 a month in model cost. If the agent works the phones, as a voice AI receptionist does, that change sits next to the telephony bill.

This guide lists the Kimi API prices per model, the caching and batch rules, the recharge tiers and rate limits, the web search tool prices and the K2 retirement, then works one monthly cost.

Kimi API prices per million tokens

Kimi inference "is billed on a pay-as-you-go basis, with no subscription plan". All K3 series models have a context window of 1,048,576 tokens; K2 series models have 262,144.

ModelInput per 1MOutput per 1MCached input per 1MCache write, 5 min / 1 hour
kimi-k3.1-pro$2.00$10.00$0.20$2.00 / $4.00
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed$4.00$20.00$0.20$4.00 / $8.00
kimi-k3$3.00$15.00$0.30$3.00 / $6.00
kimi-k2.7-code (retiring)$0.95$4.00$0.19not listed
kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed (retiring)$1.90$8.00$0.38not listed
kimi-k2.6 (retiring)$0.95$4.00$0.16not listed

The newest model is also cheaper than the one before it: kimi-k3.1-pro lists at two thirds of kimi-k3's prices, $2.00 against $3.00 input and $10.00 against $15.00 output. The highspeed variant doubles the K3.1 Pro input and output price, while its cached input stays at $0.20.

Context caching and the batch API

Two rules lower the bill:

  • Caching is automatic. "The Kimi API automatically enables context caching billing for repeated request prefixes, with a default TTL (time-to-live) of 5m." A cache hit on K3.1 Pro costs $0.20 per million input tokens, 10% of the $2.00 input price. Writing to the cache costs the input price for a 5-minute entry and twice that for a 1-hour entry.
  • Batch at 60%. "kimi-k3.1-pro and kimi-k3 support batch inference for large-scale tasks that do not require real-time responses, billed at 60% of the standard price." That is a 40% discount, smaller than the 50% batch discounts some other model APIs publish.

For an agent with a long fixed system prompt, caching does most of the work. On our arithmetic, if 15 million of 20 million monthly input tokens on K3.1 Pro were cache hits, the input side would fall from $40.00 to $13.00, before the cost of cache writes.

Recharge tiers and rate limits

Kimi sets rate limits by how much an account has topped up in total. From the recharge and rate limits page: "a minimum recharge of $1 is required to start using the API; when your cumulative recharge reaches $5, you receive a $5 voucher."

TierCumulative rechargeConcurrencyRequests per minuteTokens per minuteTokens per day
Tier0$113500,0001,500,000
Tier1$10151002,000,000Unlimited
Tier2$20401003,000,000Unlimited
Tier3$100502003,000,000Unlimited
Tier4$1,000602004,000,000Unlimited
Tier5$3,0001003005,000,000Unlimited

Tier0 is a test tier: 3 requests a minute is at most 4,320 requests a day on our arithmetic, and the 1.5 million token daily cap would cover about 600 conversations of 2,500 tokens. A $10 total top-up moves an account to Tier1 with 100 requests a minute and no daily token cap, which we suggest as the first step for a production agent.

Web search and fetch tool prices

Agents that look things up pay per tool call on top of tokens. The web search pricing page lists:

  • Web Search Basic: $0.002 per call.
  • Web Search Pro: $0.003 per call.
  • URL Fetch: $0.002 per call.

A search call is billed only when the "Request succeeds (HTTP 200) and search_results is non-empty", and a fetch only when the returned page text is not blank. A research agent that makes 10 Basic searches per lead would add $0.02 per lead, or $200 for 10,000 leads, on our arithmetic.

K2 retirement: what changes and what it costs

The pricing page carries this notice: "starting October 31, 2026, K2 series models will no longer be available to newly registered users; existing users are not affected. We plan to retire all K2 series models by the end of December 2026, please prepare your migration in advance." No exact shutdown day is given.

For a team on K2 the nearest replacement on price is kimi-k3.1-pro. Its context window is about four times larger (1,048,576 against 262,144 tokens), and its prices are about 2.1 times higher on input and 2.5 times on output, on our arithmetic. We suggest testing the agent's prompts on K3.1 Pro now, keeping the fixed prompt as a stable prefix so automatic caching applies, and moving offline jobs such as transcript summaries to the batch API at 60%.

What 10,000 conversations a month cost on Kimi

A hypothetical example: a chatbot or sales agent with 10,000 conversations a month, 2,000 input and 500 output tokens each, so 20 million input and 5 million output tokens. Our arithmetic on Kimi list prices, without caching:

ModelInput costOutput costMonthly total
kimi-k2.6 (retiring)$19.00$20.00$39.00
kimi-k3.1-pro, batch$24.00$30.00$54.00
kimi-k3.1-pro$40.00$50.00$90.00
kimi-k3$60.00$75.00$135.00
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed$80.00$100.00$180.00

With 15 million of the input tokens read from cache, K3.1 Pro would come to about $63.00 before cache writes. Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3 are also sold by Together AI at the same standard prices, with a US geo-pinned option at 25% more; see our Together AI pricing guide. For how the model bill fits into the full cost of a chatbot, see AI chatbot costs for a business. Our earlier coverage of the K3 launch is in Kimi K3 lands at 2.8 trillion parameters, and other model prices are in our AI model API pricing comparison, Qwen API pricing and DeepSeek API pricing.
